CONTROL GUIDE

Flying the Spirit

Mouse
Manual flight: steer left and right; up to climb, down to descend, centred to hold your height.
Scroll · + −
Throttle. Scroll down adds power.
A + scroll
Selected altitude in 1,000 ft steps up to the 50,000 ft ceiling, same direction as throttle. Both autopilots fly it.
1
Heading hold. Keeps course and altitude and frees the mouse for the MFDs.
2
NAV autopilot. Follows the route, flies attack runs on each objective and flies the approach.
G
Landing gear. Gear down limits speed to 250 kt; leaving it down for more than 30 s away from the field (beyond 15 km or above 6,000 ft) damages the airframe.
L
Takeoff assist: rotates at the takeoff speed (145 kt) and climbs to 1,000 ft, then switches off; climb on with the mouse or an autopilot. The gear is never automatic: G raises and lowers it.
P
Approach mode (Easy and Medium): available inside the approach corridor (final 15 km, 2.5 km either side of the centreline) at or below 5,000 ft. It descends to 250 ft and holds 150 kt; you steer (or NAV does) and lower the gear. Past the piano keys the throttle is yours: throttle back and it descends to touchdown. On Hard it sets NAV home and shows the GLIDE cue.
SPACE
Release the confirmed weapon configuration.
F
Call or disconnect the KC-135.
U
Auto refuel support on or off. With it on and an autopilot engaged, the autopilot joins the tanker once it is in view, connects, fills the tanks and disconnects. Press 1, 2 or U during auto refuel to disconnect and take over by hand.
T
Target camera on the right MFD, also in manual flight.
C
Deploy the armed countermeasure (CMS on the right MFD: SET picks a slot, ENT arms it). Toggles (STL, EMC, SIG, AUT) switch on and off.
J
Radar jammer shortcut, if JAM is loaded: threat rings have no effect while it runs. Easy 15 s × 8, Medium 10 s × 6, Hard 5 s × 2; each press spends a charge.
N
Afterburner: Mach 2 for 10 s on Easy, 8 s on Medium, 5 s on Hard, to break out of a threat ring, outrun a missile or clear the burst of a weapon released too low or too slow. Uses: 4 on Easy, 3 on Medium, 1 on Hard. Each use stresses the airframe: on Hard it goes straight to red; on Medium the first use costs nothing, the second takes the SYS outline to yellow, the third to red; on Easy the third goes yellow and the fourth red. The right MFD opens the ENG page with the throttles past 100% in blue and the burn countdown. Each burn costs a big slice of fuel: about 12% of a full load on Easy, 14% on Medium and 15% on Hard, more with a heavy load. Gear must be up.
[ · ]
Time warp for long legs: ] speeds up to ×2 then ×4, [ steps back to ×1. It drops back to ×1 by itself below 5,000 ft, within 75 km of Whiteman, on the approach, with a tanker joining or in contact, or with a missile in the air.
Esc · M
Pause · sound.

Version 2.0 · the globe

The whole Earth at about 1:28: 1,450 km round, so a lap of a great circle at 380 kt takes about 40 minutes (about 43 with the climb and approach). Real continents, capitals and major cities with ports, mountains, deserts, forests and polar ice. Weather: pick CALM, ROLLING, STORMY or CLEAR on the planning screen (NEW rolls a fresh random set). Weather systems drift round the globe like the day and night: mid-latitude fronts and lows roll east on the westerlies, tropical cells drift west, and storms breed near the equator. Between them the sky is clear; inside them you get cloud, overcast, rain and thunderstorms with lightning and turbulence. The planning globe shows the systems, and the MAP shows rain in green and storm cores in yellow and red. The sun is fixed over one side of the globe: local time follows longitude, so flying east or west takes you through dawn, day, dusk and night; near the poles the sun stays low. Headings, the HUD, RDR legend and heading tape show true heading; the MAP is north up and zooms out to 288 km. You start full of fuel. Fuel burn depends on the difficulty and the load: for one lap expect about 1 refuel on Easy, 2 on Medium (one each side) and 4 to 6 on Hard. F calls the tanker for your side of the globe: SHELL 21 (grey) east of Whiteman, TEXACO 11 (gunmetal) west of it. Airfields: Whiteman AFB (home), Edwards, Nellis, RAF Fairford, Lajes, Keflavik, Diego Garcia, Andersen, RAAF Amberley and Yokota (a game base), each with its runway on its real true heading. Free Flight can start from any of them. Within 45 km of an airfield the game switches to that airfield's frame and you can land on it; the landing end is the one facing the side you arrive from, and NAV joins the approach on your side of the final (or straight in if you are already lined up). Approach lines only show once a destination is picked on APT or HOME, or on the way home. Missions: GLOBAL ORBIT flies one great circle east and back to Whiteman; LIVE MISSIONS are the real B-2 combat sorties (Allied Force 1999, Enduring Freedom 2001, Iraqi Freedom 2003, Odyssey Dawn 2011, the Sirte camps 2017, the Houthi bunkers 2024 and Midnight Hammer 2025) with their targets, preferred stores, threats and a route that follows the real one, each timed for the local night of the strike; FREE FLIGHT goes anywhere and NAV brings you home. GAME SORTIES bring the v1 sorties to the globe: Glass Horizon (three hard targets in Marie Byrd Land) and Last Light (a nuclear airburst over a test city on the polar ice) out of Whiteman and back, and two short ones of 10 to 15 minutes, Silent Watch (Andersen to Yokota, a patrol orbit over the Pacific) and False Echo (three decoys over radar platforms out of Diego Garcia). Their threat rings sit only where no country does. Threat rings only sit inside the country being struck, never in a country allied with Australia, the UK or the US, and never near a landing airfield. Ground defence and countermeasure settings apply to live missions. Version 1.59 with the four fictional theatres is kept as a separate artifact.

Sortie

Take off at about 85% throttle; T/O assist rotates at 145 kt and climbs to 1,000 ft, then you climb on; raise the gear with G (it is never automatic). Landing: on Easy and Medium pick AUTO DESCENT (either autopilot comes down the approach profile) or AUTO LAND (NAV flies the approach and the speed) on the planning screen, and use APR (P) once you are in the approach corridor below 5,000 ft. You always lower the gear yourself. On Hard you manage the descent yourself: follow the GLIDE cue with A + scroll, then turn the autopilot off on final and fly the glide path with the mouse. Complete the objectives, then land on runway 36 at 120–160 kt with the gear down and more than BINGO (12%) fuel left. Refuelling is optional but needed on the long routes, and earns a bonus. Airframe damage: VNE is 420 kt (red band on the HUD speed tape). Flying above it, or with the gear down away from the field, wears the airframe: the SYS outline goes green, yellow at 34%, red at 67%, and at 100% the aircraft breaks up and the sortie fails. Continuous abuse destroys it in 180 s on Easy, 120 s on Medium, 60 s on Hard. Damage stays for the sortie and costs points.

Ground defences: every threat ring is a defended site. Symbols on RDR: ◎ EWR early warning, ◉ RAD search radar, ◇ TRK tracking radar, △ SAM, ▲ IR SAM, ✣ AAA guns, ))) JMR radar jammer, ▣ CMD command post, ? unidentified, → missile in flight. Dim yellow is idle, yellow is searching, flashing yellow is tracking you, red with ! is engaging. Radars see you by signature: low on the planned route, rising off it, higher with the bays open or the gear down, halved below 4,000 ft, hidden while the jammer runs. A SAM fires once its site has a full track (TRK and an EWR alert speed that up). Radar SAMs: use JAM, beam them (fly at right angles) or turn away and run before they reach you; on Hard only the jammer reliably breaks lock. IR SAMs and guns sit near targets and some sites: they ignore the jammer but cannot reach above 15,000 ft (IR) or 9,000 ft (guns). A JMR fills your scopes with noise and denies the release crosshair inside 9 km. On Hard a CMD post shares tracks between every site until it is destroyed, and contacts show ? until you get close or they emit. Stores that land on a site destroy it (200 points, CMD 600). Threat rings can be bombed out: on the left MFD RDR page press ENT to make the nearest threat site ahead the weapon target (magenta TGT brackets on RDR and MAP; ENT again drops it), then fly the release cue and release with SPACE. A hit on the radar compound at the ring centre takes the ring down for the rest of the sortie: no spike, MAP grain or nav loss, its RAD and TRK are destroyed and its SAM is blind unless a CMD network feeds it (300 points). This works with ground defence OFF too. The RDR page shows a countdown box: IMPACT time for the nearest incoming missile (with IN CHF or FLR RANGE when your chaff or flares will work), LAUNCH time while a SAM builds its track on you, and AAA FIRING under the guns. Hits add to airframe damage; at 100% you are shot down. Easy: EWR, RAD, SAM, AAA. Medium adds TRK, JMR, IR SAM. Hard adds CMD and unidentified contacts. GROUND DEFENCE on the planning screen: ON uses the set for the difficulty; OFF keeps the threat rings, radar spikes and jamming but nothing tracks or fires; CUSTOM sets how many of each type (nearest the planned route first; click a symbol to switch that type fully on or off) and whether contacts start unidentified. Missile strength and launch rate still follow the difficulty.

Countermeasures (CMS): pick up to 4 on Easy, 3 on Medium, 2 on Hard on the planning screen; the order you pick them is SET1 to SET4. Uses shrink with difficulty. JAM radar jammer (8 × 15 s / 6 × 10 s / 2 × 5 s). STL stealth mode: lights out, signature ×0.6, RDR limited to 20 km (300/200/120 s). DCY decoy: radar missiles in flight, and launches for 10 s, may chase it (4/3/2). CHF chaff: breaks radar missiles inside 3.5 km, so fire it late (12/8/5). FLR flares: breaks IR missiles inside 4 km (12/8/5). ECM: wide jamming that breaks every radar lock and collapses tracks, but alerts the network and raises your signature for 20 s after (3 × 20 s / 2 × 15 s / 1 × 10 s). EMC emissions control: signature ×0.45, RDR blank, no tanker calls (240/160/90 s). EVS evasive: assisted break to beam the nearest missile, 3,000 ft descent, a chance to shake missiles inside 6 km (4/3/2). SIG signature control: radar ×0.7, IR ×0.5, throttle capped at 70% (300/200/120 s). TOW towed decoy: radar missiles closing inside 3 km may take it, survives 2 hits (2/1/1). RWR: strobes to every radar on you, contacts identified as they illuminate, full launch calls. AUT auto defence: fires your loaded DCY, TOW, CHF or FLR at each launch, using two CHF or FLR per call.

The clock depends on difficulty: Hard 10 min, Medium 14 min, Easy 20 min. Difficulty sets how fast the ground moves away from the airfield.

Payload

Two bays, one store type each, up to the published B-2 counts (80 Mk 82, 34 CBU, 16 JDAM, 8 GBU-37, 16 JSOW or JASSM, 16 B61 or B83, 2 GBU-57). Weight raises fuel burn, lengthens the takeoff roll and slows the climb; it eases as stores go.

Any store can be loaded for any mission. Each bay is marked PREFERRED, SUITABLE or NO EFFECT ON OBJECTIVE for the mission you picked. Preferred stores earn a bonus on every hit; suitable ones complete the objective for less; the rest are dead weight against it.

Bombing

Release whenever you like, but only stores that land on an objective score. Each store falls forward of the aircraft: the faster you fly, the further it is thrown and the earlier you must release, and the smaller the margin for error. Slow down for an easier, later release. Height throws further too; guided bombs gain margin from height, free-fall bombs scatter more, so drop those low and slow. JSOW glides further the higher you launch; JASSM launches from up to 45 km within 70° of the nose. Mk 82, Mk 62 and CBU cannot defeat hardened sites. The target camera (STR / TCAM on the bottom of the right MFD, or T) shows the predicted impact cross sliding along your track toward the target and calls IN RANGE when it is inside the window. After the nuclear release, hold heading.

Theatres and targets

Four theatres: Kestrel, Sable Gulf (desert across a gulf), Trident Sea (ocean, straits and a naval coast) and Meridian (four continents). Deep sites under rock need a GBU-37 or GBU-57 with a delay fuze (a MOP does it in one hit, GBU-37s in two). Area targets take any conventional store; cluster stores count double. Ships move, so the crosshair leads them; QUICKSINK homes on a ship. Mine zones need Mk 62 mines dropped inside the dashed circle, two at a time on SINGLE or four on PAIR. On Easy and Medium the weapons computer picks the store and fuze for each target.

The corridor

The planned route is safe. Leave it to cut corners and the navigation map fills with static, NAV drops out and your signature climbs, faster inside radar rings and slower when low. At 100% you are detected and the sortie fails. Use rivers, coasts and towns to find your way back.

MFDs

MFD layout V3: top-row parent buttons open a menu of five pages beside SET1 to SET5: SET picks, SET again or ENT opens, CONT moves. Pages marked NOT FITTED are placeholders. The MODE rocker (bottom left) goes back to the menu (PAGE) and returns to the last page (CTRL); on a page, SET keeps that page's own controls. Left top: NAV (FPL flight plan: SET1 AUTO the mission plan, SET2 MAN enter your own point by point; TGT manual targets; APT airfields; VSD; HSI not fitted), TSD (TAC, RDR, RWR, TER, WXR), RDR (radar direct), COM (RAD, DCL, AWACS, MSG, FRQ), MIS (SET1 STG mission stages; SET2 LOG flight log: time of day and every key event, with SUMMARY, EVENTS, WEAPONS and FUEL tabs on SET1 to SET4 and CONT to scroll back). Left bottom 2: FMS, the Flight Management System (AUT autopilot, T/O, APP, TNK tanker, ROUTE). On the FMS menu T/O and APP are on/off switches: SET picks, ENT turns the mode on or off and the menu stays up showing ON or OFF. FMS, TNK opens the tanker page (moved from the left side button): AUTO INTERCEPT, PLOT COURSE and TANKER POSITION beside SET1 to SET3, ENT engages. Left side: Z+, Z−, NUC, two free buttons. Left bottom: MAP, FMS, RWR (threat detection), CAM (boom camera; opens on its own when a tanker is called), ENT. NAV, TGT: five target slots beside SET1 to SET5, CONT down for more (15 in all). SET picks a slot, then type LAT/LONG on the keyboard with the number keys, '.' and '-', and '/' between them (38.7/-93.5); Enter or ENT saves, Esc cancels, Backspace deletes. While typing, the number keys go to the entry, not the autopilot. A saved point is an open target (MT1 and on): it shows on MAP and RDR, can be the weapon target, and ROUTE can add it; ENT on a saved slot flies NAV direct to it. Manual targets are optional and never hold up the mission. K turns the impact cue on and off: a dotted blue line off the nose to where the selected store would land if released now, with a solid circle the size of its lethal radius (glide and cruise stores show the end of their reach). It needs no target, so it works for free drops too. Free Flight, HOSTILE AIRSPACE (planning screen): fictional scenarios on real geography over 20 cities in Russia, China, Iran, North Korea, Syria and Belarus, each built in its own local style. Per country, TARGETS adds optional objectives round every city (SAM, RDR early-warning radar, AFB airfield, COM communications, DEP depot, CMD command at capitals, CTY the city itself, which only a nuclear store affects; a B61 or B83 burst destroys every hostile objective and threat site inside its blast radius, 2.5 or 3.2 km). DEFENCES adds threat rings and ground defences: one ring per city on Easy, overlapping rings on Medium, dense rings on Hard, never near a landing airfield. TTS, RDR and the target list show them; they never hold up the sortie. Bombs leave lasting damage sized to each store's lethal radius (the same radius the hit check uses): craters with thrown-out soil, sand or snow, cracked slabs on concrete, a heaved ring for the GBU-37 and GBU-57, cluster pockmarks, a splash and slick at sea, wrecked and burning buildings in towns, and a burnt-out scar from a nuclear burst. Fires die down over about a minute; the scars stay for the sortie. RWR (left bottom 3, right bottom 2, or TSD, RWR): heading-up threat detection with the B-2 in the middle and one triangle per threat site, named by system (SA-6, SA-10, SA-21; U until identified). Yellow is a search radar painting you, orange a track or lock, red flashing a missile launch (red dots are missiles in the air); dim triangles are briefed sites not emitting. Off-scale threats sit on the rim with an arrow. SET1 THREAT (all), SET2 SEARCH, SET3 TRACK, SET4 LAUNCH filter the display; Z+ and Z− (left) or CONT (right) set the range, 5 to 80 km. FMS, AUT: SET1 NAV, SET2 HDG (keys 2 and 1 still work), SET3 TGT target list, SET4 HOME, SET5 STEER (steerpoint page); ENT engages. FMS, ROUTE: build your own flight plan. SET1 cycles the entry type (WPT waypoint, APT airfield, TGT target, AAR tanker point); SET2 edits LAT (or picks the airfield or target), SET3 edits LONG; CONT changes the active value, Z+ and Z− set the step (10, 1 or 0.1 degrees); SET4 adds the entry after the cursor, SET5 deletes the one under it; with no field active CONT moves the cursor. ENT loads the plan into NAV; if the last entry is an airfield it becomes the destination. Right top: HUD, ENG (IND, LIM, FUL, XFR, ENV), FUEL, SYS (AIR airframe, HYD, ELE, FLT, DMG), INFO (nine pages). Right side: Z+ and Z− (TCAM zoom ×1, ×2, ×4; RWR range on the left MFD), three free buttons. TTS (Threat Targeting System, right bottom 2, where RWR was) lists every threat site and open target inside 80 km, highest risk first (threats emitting at you and rings you are inside rank top; the next target on the route next). CONT moves the cursor, ENT makes that entry the weapon target: the release cue, bomb steering and TCAM move to it from the planned target; ENT on the designated entry (◆) hands it back. SET1 LIST, SET2 COORD (lat, long, bearing, range, time), SET3 PRIORITY (why it ranks there), SET4 EFFECTS (your weapon against it, release status, blast zone). Right bottom: WPN (STR, TGT, BMB weapon select, REL, FUZ), TTS (threat targeting), TCAM, CMS, ENT.

Left MFD, always live: MAP (Z+ and Z− zoom), RDR (heading-up threat display: SAM rings, targets, route ahead; Z+ and Z− step its range 10 to 160 km), MIS (the mission's key stages with a short summary each; the current one carries live guidance, CONT steps through the rest), and CAM, the boom camera. The airframe schematic (damage, gear, bays, engines, refuel door, oil and hydraulics, weapons safe or armed) is now on the right MFD under SYS, AIR. FMS holds what the bottom row used to: AUT for NAV and HDG, and T/O and APP for the takeoff and landing page (takeoff and landing: SET1 picks T.O ASSIST, SET2 picks APPROACH, ENT engages or turns off the picked mode and shows its screen; L and P stay as shortcuts), and ARF (left side, fourth button; was TNK) opens the tanker page (pick with SET1–3 or CONT, ENT engages: AUTO INTERCEPT and PLOT COURSE on Easy and Medium, TANKER POSITION on any difficulty); press a lit mode again to turn it off. NAV opens the navigation page, one option beside each of SET1 to SET5: NAV (fly the route, every waypoint and target), WPT (every point of the flight plan in order: CONT moves the cursor, ENT flies NAV direct to it and then on round the rest of the route), TGT (the mission targets in flight plan order beside SET1 to SET5, five to a page, CONT moves down and turns the page: SET picks, ENT flies NAV direct to it), APT (the airfields by distance beside SET1 to SET5, five to a page: SET picks one, ENT sets it as the destination and NAV flies its approach) and HOME (NAV direct to Whiteman); ENT (bottom right) engages the picked option, and ENT on the active one turns NAV off. Key 2 still engages NAV on the route. NUC is reserved for the nuclear launch function. On the autopilot page CONT moves a cursor down the route and ENT flies NAV direct to that steerpoint. The weapon target is set on the right MFD (TGT).

Right MFD: HUD (the PFD page), FUEL under ENG, FUL (SET1 calls the KC-135, SET2 auto refuel), ENG (shown on the runway at launch), CAM (boom camera, bottom row) and INFO (top right: environment, objectives, controls, threat key). Under the WPN menu, weapon select (BMB), REL, FUZ and TGT unlock with an autopilot; the SET button beside a row picks it. STR (stores) is under WPN too. TCAM is the target camera, CMS opens the countermeasures page: your loaded countermeasures sit beside SET1–SET4; SET picks one, ENT (bottom right) arms it and C deploys it. JAM, if loaded, also fires with J: for a short time threat rings have no effect on MAP, RDR or your signature (Easy 15 s × 8, Medium 10 s × 6, Hard 5 s × 2; a charge is used wherever you fire it); on the right MFD, DAY shows it as white day TV with blue crosshairs and NGT as green night FLIR. CONT (bottom right rocker) steps the MIS stages on the left MFD and pages through INFO, FUEL and ENG on the right. The DAY / NGT rocker (top left of each MFD) sets that display: NGT is the green screen, DAY the same symbology on black.

Communications and clock

Refuelling: about 10 s before contact the receptacle door turns over to show the red inlet and the slipway lights come up warm; both go back 5 s after disconnect.

Top left, messages from HQ, AWACS, the tanker (SHELL21 or TEXACO11, picked under TANKER on the planning screen), the tower and your own systems; HISTORY scrolls back. Top right, flight time, time to the weapon target and time to impact (counts down once a store is released), with altitude and speed below; nuclear missions also run a launch countdown to the close of the release window.

Refuelling

Manual flight. Close on the boom at 260 kt (about 52%) and 22,000 ft. Fuel flows only while aligned in the box and within 18 kt of the tanker. Or turn on auto refuel support (U, or AUTO REFUEL on the planning screen) and keep an autopilot engaged: it joins, refuels and disconnects for you.

DEBRIEF

Sortie complete.
